title: Introduce graceful batch preemption and KV checkpointing protocol
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Our continuous batcher and KV cache currently assume long-lived slot ownership. When the scheduler preempts or migrates slots (for thermal, autoscaling, or dedicated bursts), we either drop in-flight KV state or perform a heavy synchronous migration which spikes tail latency. This ticket introduces a lightweight checkpointing protocol plus a graceful preemption handshake so batch lanes can be preempted and resumed without high latency spikes or correctness regressions.

Goals: (1) Add per-slot checkpoint snapshots of hot KV entries and in-flight prefix segments; (2) Implement a preemption handshake between scheduler and batch worker to allow asynchronous checkpoint flush and fast detach; (3) Provide an atomic resume path that rehydrates KV state on a new slot with bounded staleness; (4) Add observability for checkpoint size, flush latency, resume latency, and a canary rollout plan.

Non-goals: This does not change global eviction policy, quantization logic, or persistent on-disk compaction strategy (those are separate follow-ups). It also does not attempt full-consistency distributed KV replication — we use checkpoint+lease semantics for bounded correctness suitable for inference workloads.
acceptance_criteria: Canary deployment at 10% traffic shows no increase in 95th/99th token latency beyond 5% compared to baseline
Checkpoint flush rate and size reported in Console for each slot; thresholds configurable
In-flight sessions survive preemption and resume with identical top-k tokens for determinism-sensitive tests
Automated chaos test where scheduler evicts 50% of slots at peak shows <3% request error rate and graceful retries
Documented migration plan and feature flag to disable checkpointing per cluster
implementation_steps: Design protocol - handshake messages, lease semantics, checkpoint format (in-memory delta + compacted segment)
Add lightweight serializer for hot KV entries and prefix segments; ensure memory-bound buffering
Extend scheduler API with PREEMPT-INIT and PREEMPT-COMMIT phases and timeout semantics
Implement async flush worker in batch runtime to persist checkpoint to shard store (S3-like or local mmap depending on deployment)
Implement resume path: validate checkpoint TTL, rehydrate KV into new slot, reconcile with live cache eviction policy
Add metrics and tracing (checkpoint.size, checkpoint.flush_ms, resume.ms, preempt.wait_ms), and console dashboards
Write unit + integration tests (simulated preemption, TTL expiry, hotkey correctness), and a chaos test to force evictions under load
Canary rollout: enable feature-flagged checkpointing on staging -> 10% production -> 50% -> 100%. Monitor SLIs and rollback if thresholds breached
Run dependency upgrade for runtime-kernel 2.3 that provides safe async serialization primitives (see dependency note)
Postmortem and follow-ups: measure KV hit-rate changes, tune checkpoint frequency, consider compacted deltas for long sessions
risks: Checkpoint amplification: naive snapshots could increase network and storage I/O under high concurrency
Stale state edge cases: resuming with an expired lease may cause subtle consistency regressions for streaming prompts
Dependency upgrade risk: runtime-kernel v2.3 introduces ABI changes requiring careful test matrix across GPU drivers
Performance regressions if serialization blocks hot paths; need non-blocking serializers and backpressure
Operational complexity: more moving parts for Dedicated and Private installs; require clear feature flagging and admin controls
